findings.title: Function/class edge resolution contradicts the read discipline and is unspecified
findings.description:
Section 6 resolves function- and class-level edge endpoints "to their owning file's layer rather than dropped". The architecture says "function- and class-level nodes are not read", and the slice plan says "read only file-level node types and skip function/class nodes". The design itself claims the discipline is unchanged (lines 282-289) and that "no function- or class-level node is read" (criterion 9, lines 332-333).

- **Mechanism missing:** the design does not say how the owning file is found (parsing the type-prefixed `id`, following `contains` edges, or reading the node's `filePath`). The verified-facts table suggests function nodes may not carry `filePath` at all.
- **Edge-type scope inconsistent:** the same paragraph limits the inter-layer view to `imports` and `depends_on`, then counts `calls` edges as inter-layer signal.
- **Ordering undefined:** "descending count, ties by `weight`" does not say how a per-edge `weight` aggregates for a layer pair. `edges[].direction` is listed under Interfaces Required (line 86) but appears in no mapping row.

Either drop function/class endpoint resolution (the lighter option, and what the architecture requires), or define an id-only resolution that reads no function/class node bodies and amend criterion 9 to match.

findings.title: File-level selector is a fail-open deny-list where the architecture defines an allow-list
findings.description:
The architecture enumerates nine file-level types and requires that upstream drift "surface as a loud failure, never as a silently thinner document". Correction 2 replaces this with `select(.type != "function" and .type != "class")`. Any node type upstream adds later, including a sub-file-granular one, is then admitted into context automatically. That is the exact failure the read discipline exists to prevent.

- **Guard is weak:** the only check is "no `filePath` → drift", which a new granular type carrying `filePath` passes.
- **Text contradicts itself:** line 151 says the selector "becomes an explicit type allow-list"; lines 158-159 say it is "stated as an exclusion rather than an allow-list deliberately". The heading defines file-level a third way ("carries a `filePath`").

Use the architecture's nine-type allow-list and report any node whose type is outside allow-list ∪ {`function`, `class`} as drift, by name and count. That still fixes the 201 → 238 undercount and makes a tenth type visible instead of silently included.

findings.title: Reading-order mapping drops `tour[].nodeIds`, losing the component-importance signal
findings.description:
The slice plan assigns 362 "`tour[]` ordering as the signal for which components matter most". The architecture's interview table names "`tour[]` node ordering" as the Solution Approach source for 363. Row 5 sources only `order`, `title` and `description`, so the section lists step titles with no link to components. Slice 361's shallow version already read `nodeIds`.

Since 363 reuses this mapping for Solution Approach (lines 299-301), the omission propagates. Add `nodeIds`, resolved to file-level `filePath`s, to row 5.

findings.title: "Closing observation" carve-out reintroduces unsourced prose
findings.description:
The design states "the fallback column has no third option" and that a document contains zero `[INFERRED]` markers. It then permits a closing sentence per section, tested "mechanically" by derivability from the table above it. The design's own example fails that test: "complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK" depends on knowing which files touch an external SDK, which no named field supplies.

This leaves the slice plan criterion "emits a gap marker rather than inferred prose" unenforced for those sentences, and forbidding `[INFERRED]` removes their only label. Either cut closing observations, or restrict them to restatements of counts and groupings in the table and replace the example.

findings.title: Fields outside preflight validation degrade to gap markers or silent omission on upstream rename
findings.description:
Preflight is "executed unchanged" and validates only top-level keys. The newly consumed fields (`tags`, `languageNotes`, `weight`, `project.*`, `analyzedFiles`) are not covered.

- **`tags`:** a rename yields "no node carries the entry-point tag — re-run /understand", which misdiagnoses drift as a stale graph.
- **`languageNotes`:** a rename is omitted silently (lines 211-213).

A cheap fix is to distinguish "field absent on every node" (drift wording) from "field present, no match".

findings.title: Corrections target 361 skill text that the 361 design does not contain
findings.description:
The 361 slice design specifies `select(.type == "file" or ...)` and does not say `nodeIds` mixes function and class nodes. Both corrections are therefore against the implemented skill text and the 943 sample, neither of which could be checked from the documents under review (361 is `not_started` here).

- **361 design left stale:** the corrections should also update the 361 design's read-discipline paragraph, or the two documents disagree.
- **Deferral claim unverified:** "the three fields 361 explicitly deferred" (line 54) is not stated in the 361 design.

findings.title: Minor inconsistencies and trimmable scope
findings.description:
- **`.understandignore` wording:** "An all-comments file (this repo's current state has 17 active lines) is reported as 'defaults only'" contradicts itself.
- **`config.json` reporting:** the only content is `outputLanguage: en`, which adds little to a comprehension document and nothing the slice plan asks for. It can be cut; `analyzedFiles` and `.understandignore` carry the coverage section.
- **Reference document:** "retain the document unchanged" (line 258) conflicts with adding a cross-reference line (lines 278-280). Criterion 11 also calls that file "non-document" though it sits under `project-documents/`.
- **Restated section:** "Read discipline, unchanged" (lines 282-293) mostly repeats 361 while describing a widened filter. It could shrink to the two actual deltas.
